mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen steadily from -22.7 to -6.6 over the past four weeks, indicating a resumption of commuting and associated weekday errands that feed retail footfall. This sustained recovery should continue to lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise or declines further even though WORKPLACES continues its upward trend over the next four weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined each week from 4.4 to 0.7, showing people spending less time at home. Once RESIDENTIAL drops below 1.0, it signals a behavioral shift toward out-of-home activity that should translate into higher retail visitation within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 1.0 percent
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined monotonically from 4.4 to 0.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following RESIDENTIAL crossing below 1.0, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward while RETAIL_REC still rises, breaking the causal link.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in TRANSIT (-23.3 to -13.4) and WORKPLACES (-22.7 to -6.6) indicates compounding normalization of commuting and transit-dependent shopping trips. The joint rise amplifies retail footfall beyond what either series alone would predict, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth rate does not exceed the growth rate implied by WORKPLACES alone, indicating no interaction effect between TRANSIT and WORKPLACES recovery.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility spikes sharply above 40 percent in a given week (as seen at t-2w and t-0w), it suggests a policy-driven or event-driven surge of outdoor gathering that substitutes for indoor retail visits, temporarily suppressing RETAIL_REC in the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds 40 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS spiked to 53.0 at t-2w and 50.3 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC growth decelerated
regime_hint: post-restriction reopening with large public events
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a PARKS spike above 40, contradicting the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed persistently positive and risen from 5.6 to 9.9 percent, reflecting stable essential-goods demand consistent with early autumn seasonal routines in Victoria. This steady essential mobility floor supports continued modest growth in overall retail activity including recreation-linked retail.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining stable or rising, indicating no seasonal co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week drop in TRANSIT of more than 15 points would indicate renewed public caution or a policy tightening event, which historically precedes a pullback in discretionary retail visits within one week as households reduce non-essential travel.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -23.3 to -13.4 over four weeks, showing no such drop currently
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within one week following a TRANSIT drop exceeding 15 points, or continues rising despite the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of rising WORKPLACES and rising GROCERY_PHARM reflects both commuting recovery and sustained errand activity; together these reinforce habitual multi-stop trips that include retail and recreation visits, producing a stronger joint uplift in RETAIL_REC than either series predicts alone.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increase over four weeks is no larger than the increase predicted by WORKPLACES alone, implying no interaction with GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of mild autumn weather in Melbourne, elevated and volatile PARKS mobility (ranging 12.7 to 53.0) reflects weather-driven outdoor diversions that temporarily compete with retail trips, but as weather cools over the coming month this diversion fades, allowing RETAIL_REC to recover and rise over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS shows high volatility between 12.7 and 53.0 over the snapshot period
regime_hint: seasonal transition into cooler autumn weather
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next four weeks even as PARKS volatility persists or weather-driven outdoor activity continues unabated.
